CMS publishes lower and upper rate bounds of 3.31 percent and 4.15 percent around the rounded 3.70 percent gross improper-payment rate.
PaymentAccuracy annual row 828 reports $3,575.09 million improper payments, a 0.037039355 improper-payment rate, the confidence label 95% to <100%, and a margin-of-error value of 0.42.

interpretation_boundaries: Published confidence limits close an uncertainty-output component; they do not disclose or validate the estimator, weights, simulation, or variance mechanics.
The 95-percent interval is statistical uncertainty around the gross improper-payment result, not a range of identified debt, collectibility, recovery, prevention, or savings.
The findings do not publish a separate confidence interval for the $2.53 billion net improper-payment estimate, so the gross interval must not be applied to the net result.
The annual-row value 0.42 has no unit or formula disclosed in the row and must not be labeled percentage points, percent, dollars, or a relative margin by inference.
Do not force the 0.42 margin-of-error field to reconstruct the rounded $3.19 billion to $4.01 billion or 3.31 percent to 4.15 percent findings intervals.
Rounded point estimates and interval endpoints cannot reconstruct unrounded estimates, weights, variance, or confidence-limit calculations.
OMB-compliant and statistically valid are publisher attestations, not a reproducible-methodology disclosure.
FY2024 is a post-methodology-change baseline comparable to FY2023 but not to earlier reporting years according to CMS.
No fraud, waste, debt, collectibility, recovery, prevention, or savings claim follows from the uncertainty outputs.

apr_custody_blocker.effect: The published-output component can close from captured findings and annual-workbook custody, but full estimation method remains open and the APR process passage remains without official binary custody.

field_review.remaining_need: Official APR custody and reproducible estimator, weighting, PDE-to-beneficiary linkage, simulation, record-treatment, variance, confidence-limit, margin-of-error, and rounding mechanics.
